text.p: Here is how major stock markets outside the United States ended on Tuesday.

LONDON - UK blue chips finished higher for the sixth-straight day but volumes remained light as investors continued to fret about politics and interest rates. The FTSE's advance was patchy, relying on strong gains in pharmaceuticals, oils, and banks to offset a broad decline in most other sectors. The FTSE 100 index closed 17.4 points higher at 4,346.1.

FRANKFURT - The German DAX ended slightly lower as profit-taking reverses early modest gains, trading volumes were generally low but dealers say strength of the dollar, together with upbeat spring report by Germany's six leading economic institutes allow German market to withstand most of overnight Dow fall. The DAX-30 index of German shares ended 7.25 points lower at 3,340.33. In post-bourse trade the DAX index stood at 3,348.90.

PARIS - French shares closed down though off their day's lows on election jitters tempered by rising prices on Wall Street and expectations the French conservatives would win snap elections called on Monday. The blue-chip CAC-40 index finished down eight points or 0.32 percent to 2,514.67.

ZURICH - Swiss shares extended the week's gains and the SMI closed at another record high. technical factors, demand from foreign investors, a generally favourable interest rate environment and a weaker dollar helped boost sentiment during the session. The broad Swiss Performance Index (SPI) rose 16.13 points or 0.54 percent to 3,006.44.

TOKYO - Tokyo stocks ended slightly lower after early gains brought on by a rebound in financial sector shares were eroded in the afternoon session, the losses were expected as the Nikkei average had risen continuously in the past five sessions. The 225-share Nikkei average closed 7.21 points or 0.04 percent lower at 18,544.45.

HONG KONG - Hong Kong stocks ended weak as prices bumped against resistance following recent gains and concerns about higher interest rates prompted some caution. The Hang Seng Index closed 45.19 points or 0.36 percent lower at 12,580.85 after falling to 12,533.73 during the session.

SYDNEY - A lightly-traded Australian share market eked out wafer thin gains by the close as traders digested a wages verdict from the the Australian Industrial Relations Commission that was largely in line with market expectations, nervous eyes now turned to Wednesday's March quarter inflation figures as players attempted to divine the Reserve Bank of Australia's monetary policy intentions. The benchmark All Ordinaries index added 1.8 points to 2,447.6.

JOHANNESBURG - South African industrial shares ended stronger in active trade on Tuesday, shaking off some nervousness from Monday's Wall Street's 43-point fall in early trade, the U.S. market was perceived to have needed a correction and its effect on the local market had been minimal anyway amid upbeat talk of a cut in South African interest rates in the next six months and a fall in the money market shortage. The Industrial index added 35.7 points to finish at 8,374.5, the Gold index went up 5.7 points to close at 1,263.3, and the All-share closed 25.9 points up at 7,065.9.
